polityNote: Republic of Botswana from independence (1966-09-30). First level: the administrative districts (district-council areas); the city and town councils (Gaborone, Francistown, Lobatse, Selebi-Phikwe, Jwaneng, Sowa) lie inside them and are treated as subordinate, as statoids and ISO 3166-2 did until 2014. Atoms are the ten districts of geoBoundaries BWA ADM1 (OpenStreetMap, 2017). Units whose outline no recorded change touches are drawn from independence; Central, South-East, Southern and North-West change in the undated ~1980 reorganisation (Tuli, Lobatse, the Chobe crown lands) and are drawn from the first dated source that shows the present layout (1981 census). Independent check (①): atom area / statoids area — Central 147,058/147,730 = 0.995, Chobe 21,133/20,800 = 1.016, Ghanzi 115,237/117,910 = 0.977, Kgalagadi 105,158/106,940 = 0.983, Kgatleng 7,636/7,960 = 0.959, Kweneng 37,099/35,890 = 1.034, North-East 5,337/5,120 = 1.042, North-West 111,791/109,130 = 1.024, South-East 1,753/1,780 = 0.985, Southern 27,426/28,470 = 0.963; North-West + Chobe 132,924 vs the 2001 census North-West 129,930 = 1.023.

sources.says: Change history 1885–2015: Tati renamed Francistown (~1961); Gaberones→Gaborone, Lobatsi→Lobatse, Tuli Block→Tuli (1969-08-15); ~1980 Tuli merged into Ngwato (Central), Lobatse district split between Gaborone (South-East) and Ngwaketse (Southern), parts of Chobe to Ngamiland and Ngwato; Chobe/North-West 2001–2006. No other boundary change.
